_what_this_is: The gate catalogue behind /government-money. It holds what is DURABLE about each kind of program — who it is for, what it is gated on, which other programs it interacts with, and the office that can confirm it — and deliberately holds NO dollar amounts, percentages, caps, thresholds or deadlines. See _why_no_amounts.
_why_no_amounts: A held figure is a figure that goes stale silently. Amounts, caps, income thresholds and deadlines are exactly the facts that change every year, and a report that prints one from a file written in September is the same defect as a model reciting one from its training data — the audit's whole finding, moved from the prompt into a JSON file. What does NOT change on that timescale is that a credit against tax owed is useless to a household that owes none, that a renter cannot claim an owner's credit, that a rebate usually reduces the basis a federal credit is computed on, and that nine states have no individual income tax. Those are what this file holds, and they are enough to decide every line. The amount is then confirmed by the customer, at the authority named on the line. tests/government-money-engine.test.js fails if any entry ever acquires a number.
_confidence: high = a long-standing, structurally stable feature of how this kind of program works. check = commonly true but varies by state, utility or year, and is written as likely-and-worth-confirming. Nothing in this file is written as settled fact about a specific current program.

authorities.federal-tax: the IRS guidance for residential energy credits — ask your tax preparer, or search irs.gov for the residential energy credit guidance for the year the work was finished
authorities.federal-vehicle: the IRS clean vehicle credit guidance, plus the dealer, who must supply a time-of-sale report
authorities.federal-benefit: benefits.gov, or the federal agency that administers the program
authorities.state-tax: your state's department of revenue or taxation
authorities.state-energy: your state energy office, or your local community action agency
authorities.state-human-services: your state department of human services — the 211 helpline will route you
authorities.county-assessor: your county auditor or assessor's office
authorities.utility: your electricity and gas providers — the names are printed on your bill
authorities.marketplace: healthcare.gov, or your state's own insurance marketplace

capGroups.fed-efficiency-annual: A federal annual aggregate for efficiency work on the home envelope and systems. Several kinds of work share one yearly ceiling, so doing three of them in one year does not produce three ceilings — and splitting work across a year boundary can produce two.
capGroups.fed-efficiency-heatpump: A separate federal annual ceiling for heat-pump equipment, which does not share with the envelope group above.

_noIndividualIncomeTax: States with no broad individual income tax, so a state income-tax credit cannot apply to a resident of one. New Hampshire is deliberately NOT on this list: it has no tax on wages but has taxed investment income, so 'no state income tax credits exist for you' would be too strong a statement to make about a New Hampshire household. Structural and stable — this is the one genuinely state-specific fact in the file, and it produces a real ruled-out line rather than a hedge.
_incomeBands: Bands, never an exact figure — nobody needs one, and most real gates are against household size and area median income rather than a flat number. A gate listed here is therefore a SCREEN, not a determination: being in a qualifying band produces 'check', not 'claim'.

programs.label: Federal home energy efficiency credit — building envelope
programs.covers: insulation, air sealing, exterior doors and windows

programs.label: Federal home energy efficiency credit — heat pumps
programs.covers: air-source heat pumps and heat-pump water heaters

programs.label: Federal home energy efficiency credit — other systems
programs.covers: efficient furnaces, air conditioners, conventional water heaters and electrical panel upgrades done as part of qualifying work

programs.label: Federal credit for a home energy audit
programs.covers: a written home energy assessment by a qualified auditor

programs.label: Federal residential clean energy credit
programs.covers: solar electric, solar water heating, battery storage, geothermal heat pumps and small wind

programs.label: Federal new clean vehicle credit
programs.covers: a qualifying new plug-in or fuel-cell vehicle
programs.note: Eligibility turns on the specific vehicle as well as the buyer — assembly location, battery sourcing and a price ceiling all apply, and in recent years the credit could be taken at the dealer instead of on the return. The dealer must give you a time-of-sale report either way; without it the credit is usually lost.

programs.label: Federal used clean vehicle credit
programs.covers: a qualifying used plug-in or fuel-cell vehicle bought from a dealer
programs.note: Private-party sales are generally excluded, and there are limits on the vehicle's age and price.

programs.label: Federal credit for home EV charging equipment
programs.covers: a charger installed at the home
programs.note: This one has a geographic condition — eligibility has been limited to homes in certain census tracts. Confirm your address qualifies before counting on it.

programs.label: Federal child tax credit
programs.covers: a qualifying child in the household
programs.note: Partly refundable, so unlike the energy credits it can be worth something even in a year with little tax owed.

programs.label: Federal child and dependent care credit
programs.covers: care you paid for so that you could work or look for work

programs.label: Federal earned income credit
programs.covers: working households under an income ceiling that rises with household size
programs.note: Refundable, so it can pay out even with no tax owed. The ceiling depends heavily on household size and on whether there are children.

programs.label: Federal education credits
programs.covers: tuition and required expenses for higher education

programs.label: Federal retirement savings contributions credit
programs.covers: money you put into a retirement account, for lower- and middle-income households

programs.label: Health insurance marketplace premium assistance
programs.covers: households buying their own health cover rather than getting it through an employer
programs.note: Assistance is applied to the premium during the year and reconciled on the return, so income changes mid-year matter.

programs.label: Your state's own version of the federal credits
programs.covers: state income-tax credits that often mirror or top up the federal energy, childcare and earned-income credits

programs.label: Property tax relief for owner-occupiers
programs.covers: homestead exemptions and the extra relief many states add for older owners, veterans and people with disabilities
programs.note: Almost always has to be applied for once rather than arriving automatically, and is often missed for years by people who already qualify.

programs.label: Renter's property tax relief
programs.covers: the renter's credit or 'circuit breaker' some states run, on the basis that rent carries property tax through it

programs.label: Weatherization assistance
programs.covers: insulation, air sealing and heating repairs done at no cost for income-qualified households
programs.note: Federally funded and delivered locally, usually through a community action agency. Renters can sometimes qualify with the owner's consent.

programs.label: Home energy bill assistance
programs.covers: help with heating and cooling bills, and in many states with a crisis shut-off

programs.label: First-time homebuyer assistance
programs.covers: down payment help, closing cost assistance and in some states a mortgage credit certificate
programs.note: A mortgage credit certificate has to be obtained BEFORE closing, which is why this one is so often missed.

programs.label: Age- or disability-based relief
programs.covers: property tax freezes and deferrals, utility discounts and transport concessions

programs.label: Veteran property tax and fee relief
programs.covers: property tax exemptions and fee waivers for veterans, often larger where a disability rating applies

programs.label: Utility rebate on efficient equipment
programs.covers: heat pumps, water heaters, furnaces, air conditioners and efficient appliances
programs.note: Very often has to be applied for within a window after installation, and the window is short.

programs.label: Utility rebate on insulation and air sealing
programs.covers: envelope work, sometimes conditional on an audit first

programs.label: Free or discounted utility energy audit
programs.covers: an assessment of the home, often with free equipment fitted on the visit
programs.note: Worth doing first where it exists: some utility rebates are only available to households that have had the audit.

programs.label: Utility rebate on thermostats and controls
programs.covers: smart thermostats and connected controls, sometimes free in exchange for enrolling in demand response

programs.label: Net metering or solar export credit
programs.covers: what your utility pays or credits for power your panels send back
programs.note: Not a rebate — an ongoing tariff, and the terms differ enormously between utilities and change for new customers.

programs.label: Income-qualified utility rate discount
programs.covers: a permanently reduced rate or a fixed monthly credit for income-qualified households
programs.note: Separate from bill assistance, and a household can usually have both.
